procedure: Descriptive. No new hypothesis test or inferential claim is introduced; Welch intervals are reused solely to visualize between-design uncertainty at bin level. Confirmatory realizations r1..r5; r0 is reported apart and never averaged into a confirmatory mean. 15 geometric bins inside the selection range; the two bins outside have no defined intended density and appear in the supplementary rows, as spillover and tail behaviour, never as truncation. Bins with fewer than STRUCTURAL_MIN_TEST_N test points are marked, never dropped, and the concordance count is primarily over the unmarked bins. Concordance is the count of bins with (delta density) x (delta log-RMSE) < 0; bins with either difference exactly zero leave the denominator. achieved - intended is the net distortion of the requested bin-count distribution, not the screener's prediction error; the displacement rows describe the screener on the points it selected, conditioned on selection, and their shift statistics cover only points whose true FOS stayed inside the selection range.
figure_caption: Per-bin training density and per-bin error, both as a difference against B, over the five confirmatory realizations. Every interval, on the density panel and on the error panels alike, visualizes variability between designs and constitutes no test; the fifteen intervals are a diagnostic, not fifteen tests. The pattern is consistent with density-driven relocation; it is not evidence that density caused it. The small numbers above the error panels are the test points per bin. Hollow markers, on the error panels, are bins with fewer than 10 of them; they are shown but carry no statement in the text. Both the densities and the errors in this figure are read from the replication metrics and use the half-open reporting zones; the allocation and displacement tables use the generator's binning instead, which differs only on an exact bin edge.
